text:
alyssa: Heads-up: I just tried the zero-config Next starter (one-click deploy) with the new LlamaIndex example and hit two onboarding issues.
micah: what happened? link?
alyssa: repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-zero-starter (local copy). Steps: npm install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, npm run dev. The app boots but auth retries flood logs and pages hang on first request.
jordan: hm, does the SDK autoswap to the host endpoint if env var missing? we've had parity issues between node sdk and python sdk before.
alyssa: SDK is present in package.json @redwood/sdk-js v0.12.1. When I inspect network calls the client does a 401 then immediate retry loop (every 200ms) until browser tab freezes. No exponential backoff.
sam: ack. That's our auth/retry default behaviour — dev build was supposed to use a 3 retry, jittered backoff. Looks like the zero-config template pins an older client config.
micah: can you paste the request headers/response? small snippet is enough.
alyssa: ```http
> POST /v1/generate
> Authorization: Bearer undefined
< 401 {"error":"missing api key"}
``` 
micah: Authorization: Bearer undefined? So env isn't injected into the client. Next publicRuntimeConfig vs serverRuntimeConfig mixup? The starter sets NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env.local but we intended server-only var REDWOOD_API_KEY.
jordan: that explains it — browser tries calling hosted API with undefined token which triggers immediate retry. Fix options: 1) proxy calls through next server to hide key (recommended for prod), 2) dev starter should set a local dev-token placeholder and client should handle missing key gracefully (non-blocking error message), 3) update sdk-js to include backoff on 401.
alyssa: for onboarding, (2) is lowest friction. Users can still click-through with a dummy key and see UI. But we also need to document the recommended secure pattern (proxy / environment). Right now the README says set REDWOOD_API_KEY but starter uses NEXT_PUBLIC_ var — mismatch.
sam: I'll open a PR to change the example to server-side use and also add a short section in README about auth patterns and the expected env names. Also will pin sdk-js to v0.12.3 which has jittered backoff on 401.
micah: nice. Also we should add a quick e2e smoke test in the repo that runs `npm run dev` and does one /api/health and one generate call (mocked) so the CI can catch regressions.
devex-bot: CI pipeline triggered: test/zero-starter-smoke (pending) — https://ci.internal/1234
jordan: small note: our eval harness docs reference a `samples/eval` prompt set; this starter uses `examples/eval` path. Minor but will break the eval-onboarding flow users click from Console -> Quickstart.
alyssa: good catch. I'll consolidate to `examples/eval` and add a tiny eval harness that runs locally (`npm run eval-local`). Should be in same PR.
sam: can we also add a short paragraph in the SDK README about retry semantics and how to override them? People hit this subtlety often.
micah: +1. Also add a debug page in the starter that prints resolved env vars server-side (but not in prod) so users can quickly see where keys are wired.
alyssa: PR #487 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-zero-starter/pull/487 — changes: server-side token, bump sdk-js, README auth section, eval harness example, smoke e2e. CI showed one flaky test on windows.
jordan: will review today. If we want a faster unblock we can land a tiny patch that replaces NEXT_PUBLIC_ with server REDWOOD_API_KEY in env example and set default dummy key for dev mode.
sam: agreed. I'll add fallback dev key in .env.example but with big warning comment.
alyssa: thanks everyone. once this lands I'll re-run the onboarding runbook and report back if any other friction pops up.
micah: thanks for catching it. small things like this make first-run experience so much better. :party_parrot:
devex-bot: PR merged: #487 — main (12 minutes ago) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-zero-starter/commit/abc123
